defects.description: escapeHtml leaves the single quote untouched, so a value inside a single-quoted attribute such as renderTitle breaks out of the attribute.
defects.why_missed: Every suite value avoids the apostrophe and the title test uses a plain word, so the one attribute context that depends on the missing character is never exercised.
defects.severity_rationale: A quote-bearing value can inject an event handler when rendered in a single-quoted attribute.
defects.failure_condition: [escapeHtml("x' onload='alert(1)"), renderTitle("x' onload='alert(1)")] -> "x' onload='alert(1)" title='x' onload='alert(1)'

detection_criteria.mechanism: escapeHtml leaves the single quote untouched, so a value inside a single-quoted attribute such as renderTitle breaks out of the attribute.
detection_criteria.proof: Show an exploitable condition, or a concrete violation of a named security property (the input and the boundary it crosses).

defects.description: escapeHtml re-escapes an ampersand that already starts an entity, so a value escaped at one layer and escaped again renders as &amp;.
defects.why_missed: The suite escapes each value once; applying the function twice is a property the contract states and no single-call test can observe.
defects.severity_rationale: Re-escaping an already escaped value changes output on a rare repeated-use input.

detection_criteria.mechanism: escapeHtml re-escapes an ampersand that already starts an entity, so a value escaped at one layer and escaped again renders as &amp;.
detection_criteria.proof: Show one input or state where the output contradicts expected_behavior.
